generalfeedback.text:
Check two things for each of Juma's points: is its height a running total, and is it plotted at an upper class boundary? The cumulative frequency at an upper class boundary counts every value below that boundary, so each running total belongs at the upper class boundary of its class, and the curve starts at \(({@exd(lcb1)@},\ 0)\). Joining the points with straight lines is fine.

[[if test="is(er=1)"]]

(a) Juma's heights go up and down: they are the frequencies \({@f@}\), not the running totals \({@cf@}\).

[[elif test="is(er=2)"]]

(a) Juma's points are at the class midpoints, such as \({@exd(mid[1])@}\) for the first class, half a class to the left of the upper class boundaries.

[[else]]

(a) Juma's points are at the lower class boundaries, such as \({@exd(lcb[1])@}\) for the first class, a whole class to the left of the upper class boundaries.

[[/if]]

(b) The class {@lo[j]@}–{@hi[j]@} has upper class boundary \({@exd(ucbj)@}\), so its cumulative frequency, \({@cf[j]@}\), is plotted at \(x = {@exd(ucbj)@}\).

questiondescription.text:
Statistics II: finding the mistake in an ogive

Grade 12 CBE Core and Essential 3.1: Identify the plotting error in a drawn cumulative frequency curve and give the correct plotting position.

Core and Essential

truefeedback.text: Straight lines are fine. Look at where each point is plotted, and at its height.

falsefeedback.text:
[[if test="is(ch=2)"]]

If Juma had plotted the frequencies, his heights would be {@sl(f)@}. They are {@sl(cf)@}: they never go down, and the last is the total, \({@n@}\). So the heights are running totals. Look at where each point is placed.

[[elif test="is(ch=3) and is(er=1)"]]

The class midpoints are {@sl(mid)@}. Juma's points are at \(x =\) {@sl(ucb)@}, the ends of the classes, so his points are in the right places. Look at their heights.

[[elif test="is(ch=3)"]]

The class midpoints are {@sl(mid)@}. Juma's points are at \(x =\) {@sl(rest(jx))@}. Compare these with the classes in the table.

[[elif test="is(ch=4) and is(er=1)"]]

The lower class boundaries are {@sl(lcb)@}. Juma's points are at \(x =\) {@sl(ucb)@}, the ends of the classes, so his points are in the right places. Look at their heights.

[[elif test="is(ch=4)"]]

The lower class boundaries are {@sl(lcb)@}. Juma's points are at \(x =\) {@sl(rest(jx))@}. Compare these with the classes in the table.

[[else]]

Check two things for each of Juma's points: is its height a running total, and is it plotted at an upper class boundary?

[[/if]]

truefeedback.text: That is the midpoint. A cumulative frequency counts every value up to the end of the class: plot at the upper class boundary.
That is the lower class boundary. By then only \({@cf[j-1]@}\) values have been counted, not \({@cf[j]@}\).
\({@hij@}\) is the upper class limit. The values are rounded to the nearest whole number, so some values a little above \({@hij@}\) also round into this class. Where does the class really end?

falsefeedback.text: A cumulative frequency is plotted at the upper class boundary of its class.
